details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- tests/test_stage_switch_watch.py:344-353 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `test_real_registry_loads_unchanged` reads `entry["stage"]` without checking that it exists, for every raw entry in scripts/stage_switches.json, but this PR makes `stage` optional.
  WHY: The first slim entry that the schema allows (e.g. `{"name": "X_ENABLED", "pending": true}`) raises KeyError: 'stage' and fails CI on a registry the loader accepts, which defeats G2/G3 of #10127. All reviewers rated it MAJOR. minimax_minimax-m3 raised the same point at line 349, but only as a hardening suggestion.
- tests/test_stage_switch_registry.py:173-176 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `test_real_registry_loads_unchanged` reads `entry["stage"]` directly from raw scripts/stage_switches.json entries, but the PR makes `stage` optional.
  WHY: A raw entry without `stage` raises KeyError: 'stage' and fails CI. This is probably the same root cause as the tests/test_stage_switch_watch.py finding, but the reviewer cites a different file, so it is not merged.
- scripts/stage_switch_watch.py:302-308 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `off_on_purpose` marker loop in `load_registry` only checks `isinstance(marker, dict)`. It does not check that the documented `pending` field is a boolean, as the switch loop does at lines 300-301, and (per minimax) it never validates `name`/`until`/`reason`.
  WHY: A marker with `pending: "yes"` loads silently with exit 0, and only tests/test_stage_switch_registry.py::test_registry_entries_are_well_formed catches it, so the loader and the test enforce different rules for the same field. Severity disagrees: minimax rated it MAJOR (a malformed registry reaches the watch, against G3), while sonnet/gemini/glm rated it NIT because runtime evaluation ignores `pending`. The highest rating is used. openai_gpt-6-luna raised the same point only as a hardening suggestion (lines 305-307).
- scripts/stage_switch_watch.py:209 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `_readme_variables_rows` stops at any line starting with `#` (`re.match(r"^#", line)`), not only at real headings.
  WHY: A stray `#` line can end table parsing early and drop later variables from discovery. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rejected this: the code was moved verbatim from the test, and neither README table has a stray `#` line.
- scripts/stage_switch_watch.py:198 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `_readme_variables_rows` table loop stops on ANY line starting with `#` (in a fenced code block, an HTML comment, or a malformed row) and silently drops every row below it.
  WHY: Switches below the stray line go unwatched with no error, and the registry test shares the same code path, so it would miss them too. This is the same root cause as the line-209 finding but is kept separate because the cited lines are more than 5 apart. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rejected it.
- scripts/stage_switch_watch.py:141-155 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `_scan_workflow_switches` uses `raw.splitlines()` followed by `"\n".join(...)` to filter comments.
  WHY: Whitespace may be normalised inconsistently between CRLF and LF files, which could make `SWITCH_DEFAULT_RE` miss multi-line expressions. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rejected this because splitlines handles \r\n and `\s` matches \n.
- scripts/stage_switch_watch.py:151 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Comment filtering in `_scan_workflow_switches` uses `line.strip().startswith("#")`.
  WHY: This simple heuristic may filter lines that are not real comments and cause false negatives in switch discovery. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rejected this: it is the same filter the test used before the PR, and the fixture tests cover it.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: Issue #10127, Tests section: "A JSON entry for an undiscovered name fails the test unless it has pending: true."
  expected_change_site: tests/test_stage_switch_registry.py (or tests/test_stage_switch_watch.py)
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  EVIDENCE: test_registry_entries_name_discovered_or_pending runs its check only inline against the real ROOT and REGISTRY. No fixture registry or fixture repo shows that an undiscovered, non-pending entry is rejected, and test_entry_detail_wins_over_discovery only shows that a pending entry loads.
- requirement: "The JSON becomes optional detail" and keeps "only what cannot be derived" per switch.
  expected_change_site: scripts/stage_switches.json
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: The PR does not modify scripts/stage_switches.json, and its entries still carry the derivable `"default": "true"` field (e.g. lines 5-6 and 11-12) even though the loader now derives it. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash rejected this gap: G4 requires the existing entries to be honoured unchanged, and per glm the plan's files_touched does not include the file.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- tests/test_stage_switch_watch.py:test_real_registry_loads_unchanged | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The loop "for entry in raw["switches"]: assert by_name[entry["name"]]["stage"] == entry["stage"]" reads raw "stage" without checking that it exists. The PR makes "stage" optional in load_registry, the module docstring, test_registry_entries_are_well_formed, README.md line 560 and agents.d/10127-stage-switch-discovery.md.
  WHY: The first slim entry added to the real registry (e.g. {"name": "X_ENABLED", "on_values": ["1"]}) raises KeyError: 'stage' and breaks G2/G3 of #10127. Fix: compare only when "stage" is present; otherwise assert the merged stage equals ssw._generated_stage_text(name, files) or starts with "Turns on ".
- scripts/stage_switch_watch.py:load_registry off_on_purpose marker loop | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Switch entries get the check "if "pending" in entry and not isinstance(entry["pending"], bool)" but markers do not, although README.md line 560 and the agents.d/10127 fragment document "pending: true" for markers.
  WHY: The runtime result is the same because _valid_markers ignores "pending", but the loader and tests/test_stage_switch_registry.py::test_registry_entries_are_well_formed apply different rules to the same field. Fix: about 2 lines that raise RegistryError on a non-bool marker pending.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: Issue #10127, Tests section: "A JSON entry for an undiscovered name fails the test unless it has pending: true."
  Expected change site: tests/test_stage_switch_registry.py (or tests/test_stage_switch_watch.py)
  Evidence of absence: test_registry_entries_name_discovered_or_pending runs only inline against the real ROOT and REGISTRY. There is no fixture that proves the check fires, so an inverted comparison would pass unnoticed.
  SEVERITY: NIT | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- Rejected pass-1 findings (4 related items): CRLF/splitlines in _scan_workflow_switches (gemini), the "#"-prefix comment filter (gemini), the "^#" break in _readme_variables_rows (minimax), and the TASK_GAP on the stage_switches.json default field (luna; G4 requires entries to be honoured unchanged).
- HARDENING (2 related items): marker pending bool check in load_registry (2 lines); "if "stage" in entry:" guard in test_real_registry_loads_unchanged (2 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

  PROBLEM: `load_registry` does not check the type of `pending` in `off_on_purpose` markers, unlike `switches` entries.
  WHY: An invalid type (e.g. `pending: "yes"`) passes validation and could cause runtime errors if the orchestrator expects a boolean.
- tests/test_stage_switch_registry.py:test_real_registry_loads_unchanged (lines 173-176) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The test reads `entry["stage"]` directly from raw registry entries, but `stage` is now optional.
  WHY: An entry without `stage` raises `KeyError: 'stage'` and fails CI.
- scripts/stage_switch_watch.py:_readme_variables_rows (line 209) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The loop stops early on any line starting with `#` (`re.match(r"^#", line)`).
  WHY: A non-heading `#` line can end table parsing and drop later variables from discovery.
- scripts/stage_switch_watch.py:_scan_workflow_switches (lines 141-155) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The scanner uses `raw.splitlines()` followed by `"\n".join(...)` to filter comments.
  WHY: Whitespace may be normalised inconsistently between CRLF and LF, which could make `SWITCH_DEFAULT_RE` miss multi-line expressions.
- scripts/stage_switch_watch.py:_scan_workflow_switches (line 151) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Comment filtering uses `line.strip().startswith("#")`.
  WHY: This simple heuristic may filter lines that are not real comments, causing false negatives in switch discovery.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "The JSON becomes optional detail" and keeps "only what cannot be derived" per switch.
  Expected change site: scripts/stage_switches.json
  Evidence of absence: The PR does not remove the derivable `"default": "true"` field from existing entries (e.g. lines 5-6 and 11-12).
  SEVERITY: NIT | ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/stage_switch_watch.py:302-308 (load_registry marker loop, vs switch loop 279-301) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `off_on_purpose` marker loop does no field-level validation. `pending: "yes"` is accepted although the switch loop enforces `isinstance(entry["pending"], bool)` at lines 300-301 and README.md:561 / agents.d/10127-stage-switch-discovery.md:2 document `pending` for markers. `name`, `until` and `reason` are never validated at load time either.
  WHY: The snapshot/evaluate commands exit 0 and use bad marker data, and only tests/test_stage_switch_registry.py::test_registry_entries_are_well_formed catches it. This defeats G3's aim of failing at load time.
- scripts/stage_switch_watch.py:198 (_readme_variables_rows, `if re.match(r"^#", line): break`) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The table loop stops on ANY line starting with `#`, not only a markdown heading, and silently drops every row below it.
  WHY: Switches below a stray `#` line go unwatched with no warning, and the registry test shares the same parser.
- HARDENING (3 related items): marker loop at lines 305-307 should reject non-bool `pending` and validate `name`/`until`/`reason` (6-8 lines, risk 2); tests/test_stage_switch_watch.py test_real_registry_loads_unchanged at line 349 should guard `entry["stage"]` with `if "stage" in entry:`, otherwise assert the merged stage starts with "Turns on " (3-4 lines, risk 1); _scan_workflow_switches at lines 159-162: splitlines/join could break matches in folded YAML blocks, so match `SWITCH_NOT_FALSE_RE` per line or add a folded-block test (2-3 lines, risk 1). Aggregate HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
